evidence.reason: The finding alleged that cap() passed through non-string parsed values (e.g. the provider/model object for CQ_SELFHOST_DRIVER, numbers, short arrays), which ProvenanceConfigSchema would reject. The current file no longer uses cap(): it defines render() (lines 29-40), which stringifies every value — strings as-is, arrays joined with commas via recursive render, {provider, model} objects as `${provider}/${model}` (preserving the provider/model format), other objects via JSON.stringify, and primitives via String(). The file header (lines 16-19) states every recorded value is a STRING so it always satisfies the strict ProvenanceConfigSchema, and the caller assigns these strings into env values. The implementation matches the suggested fix, so the defect is no longer present at the pinned tip. The change came with the schema-valid provenance recording work in 8c9e136d, whose message ('record schema-valid provenance config from the run snapshot') matches this correction; later history entries concern URL redaction/errored-snapshot refusal, not value serialization.
